findings.citation: Not graded: titles, the wording of anything, which valid decomposition you choose, extra keys, dependencies beyond the required ones (as long as wave rules hold), routing choices other than the rules stated under Routing, and test levels other than the classification stated above.
findings.description: The public instruction discloses the hidden verifier's exact exclusions, enabling candidates to optimize against check coverage rather than satisfy the full planning contract.

findings.citation: Use as few waves as the constraints allow: no task may be placeable in an earlier wave, i.e. for every earlier wave either one of its dependencies is in that wave or later, or it overlaps a task already in that wave.
findings.description: The tightness check only tests whether a task can move to an earlier wave; it accepts an otherwise valid plan with an extra empty trailing wave, although that does not use as few waves as allowed.

findings.citation: `mcp_tools` lists exactly the MCP tool names your tasks implement in `tools/kerrigan-mcp/`, written as in `spec.md` (e.g. `kerrigan.dispatch`).
findings.description: The harness converts the candidate list to a set before comparison, so duplicate tool-name entries pass even though the list is required to contain exactly the four names.

findings.citation: `tests` lists at least one test for the task's "done" condition; every entry uses the closed vocabularies below, and at least one entry has an environment other than `manual-human`.
findings.description: The check validates only entry vocabulary and the presence of a non-manual environment; it does not verify that any declared test exercises the task's done condition.

findings.citation: Decompose milestones M2–M8 into tasks that can each be dispatched to one cloud agent (one task → one issue → one PR), declare what each task touches, order them into parallel-safe waves, route each one with the delegation rubric, and map acceptance criteria to tests.
findings.description: Beyond specifically named required-touch paths, the verifier checks touch syntax and path existence but not whether a task's touch set completely and accurately declares the files needed for all covered deliverables.

findings.citation: `routing_rule` is a rule ID defined in `delegation-rubric.md` (`R-cloud-default` when no other rule fires).
findings.description: Except for pure-logic and local-attested cases, the verifier only checks membership in the routing-rule vocabulary; it accepts a non-default rule even when its rubric predicate does not fire.

publicationScope: Admission judgments and native outcome metadata only; prompts, raw streams, HTTP bodies, configuration and credential state excluded.
